extracted.intended_audience: communications/PR professionals, corporate communicators, and business owners writing new-hire press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting and distributing press releases announcing new hires (especially executives), covering headline, content, quotes, visuals, approvals, distribution, and length/readability. Aimed at creating newsworthy, media-ready announcements that align hires with company strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with a Strong Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: New hire press release headlines should grab attention immediately. Include the full name and title of the new hire, your company name and strong verbs like “welcomes,” “appoints,” or “announces.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A straightforward and powerful approach communicates key information and sets a positive tone. Example: “Tech Innovator XYZ Corp Welcomes Jane Smith as New Chief Technology Officer.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Confirm the Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the full name, position title, start date and a brief mention of previous years of experience, key accomplishments and relevant industry background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak directly with the new hire to confirm details, get new hire quotes, and run the release by the new hire’s superior or department head for approval to avoid errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow AP Style and Standard Press-Release Template
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release for a new employee announcement follows a similar template as other topics. Make sure you focus on the newsworthy aspects of your announcement and follow AP Style guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard press release structure and AP Style for consistency and journalist friendliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Goals in Addition to Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear job description but go beyond listing responsibilities by talking about specific projects or improvements they’ll work on and how they’ll contribute to the company’s long-term success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help readers understand the strategy behind the hire; concrete goals and projects make the hire more newsworthy and meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect to Your Company Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the hire within the larger context of your company’s direction and achievements; explain how they align with your mission and show how they’ll help drive your vision forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to demonstrate culture fit and reinforce company values—this helps earn positive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate to the Real World / Industry Trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Create interest by connecting the hire to larger market or industry trends, or local impacts (e.g., job creation). If replacing a high-profile individual, note that context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: hiring a sustainability expert can be tied to climate commitments; a factory lead can be tied to job creation and economic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look to the Future / Use Forward-Looking Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a glimpse of what this new position means for the future and position your company as a leader, disruptor or emerging player in your industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a forward-looking quote from the CEO or another company leader expressing excitement about the hire and its implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make It Visual
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a professional headshot of your new hire and other multimedia (videos, logos, office photos, audio clips) to make the announcement more engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia can substantially increase views—PR Newswire cites up to six times more views—so include images and/or video when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always Give Contact Information and Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: New hire press release templates always include a press release boilerplate and media contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an easily reachable media contact for follow-ups and include a company boilerplate to give journalists context about the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Appropriate Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from the new hire and a company leader (and when relevant, a board member) to add credibility and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes to articulate vision, enthusiasm, strategic fit, or expected impact; tailor who is quoted to the hire type (e.g., board member for nonprofit executive director).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor Content to the Type of Hire
rubrics_metrics.description: Different hires require different emphases: executives — highlight expertise and alignment with company goals; executive directors — highlight passion for the cause and sector experience; CEO — background, achievements and vision; mass hiring — explain hiring reason and include application link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tone, detail level, and included elements (e.g., board quotes for nonprofits, application links for bulk hires) to the announcement type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize Newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the newsworthy aspects of your announcement so it will attract media interest; executive hires are typically more newsworthy but other angles (trend alignment, mass hiring) can make announcements newsworthy too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, frame the hire as strategic, tied to market shifts, community impact, or company milestones to increase pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for 400–600 words for a new employee press release to include necessary information without overwhelming readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise language, break up text with subheadings, and focus on the most important details about the new hire and their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Social Media to Amplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Use social media to amplify your new hire announcements and extend reach beyond distribution lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share quotes, headshots, and multimedia on social platforms to increase visibility among job seekers, influencers, and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Clear Calls to Action for Hiring Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: When announcing mass hiring or recruitment drives, include why the hiring is happening now and provide a link where readers can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain context (expansion, seasonal needs, new location) and make it easy for interested candidates to take immediate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Distribution and Amplification Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage distribution networks and services (e.g., PR Newswire) to get your announcement into newsrooms, websites, journalists and influencers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution services can increase reach, social shares, and engagement; consider paid distribution or value-added services to maximize coverage.
